10.3.2 nutritional properties of CHinese Vinegar
10.3.2.1 Amino Acids
Vinegar contains 0.005–0.5% of total nitrogen, of which amino acids account for
```
45–50% (Alvarez-Caliz et al., 2014). More than 16 different free amino acids, gen-
```
erated through protein degradation of the raw materials, have been determined in
```
Chinese vinegar (Chen et al., 2013b; Li et al., 2016b; Wang et al., 2016). These amino
```
acids are part and parcel of the specific nutritional value, color, and flavor of Chinese
vinegar. First of all, essential amino acids are included in vinegar and can supple-
```
ment the diet to help meet nutritional requirements (Chen et al., 2013b; Wu et al.,
```
```
2013). Moreover, amino acids (such as lysine, histidine, arginine) and sugars in the
```
vinegar brewing process generate melanoidins by Maillard reactions to increase the
```
color of end-products (Morales et al., 2012). In addition, amino acids are important
```
taste components, such as glycine, alanine, and proline with sweet taste, leucine,
arginine, methionine, and tryptophan with bitter taste, aspartate and glutamic acid
with sour taste, and sodium aspartate and sodium glutamate with umami sensations
```
(Chen and Zhang, 2007; Ley, 2008; Zhao et al., 2003).
```
Furthermore, glutamic acid, alanine, valine, aspartate, lysine, and proline are the
principal components in Chinese vinegars, among amino acids, to confer mellow
and soft flavors, in addition to the possibility to help distinguish raw materials and
production methods in different brands. Alanine, glycine, and proline were found
to be characteristic amino acid components in Shanxi aged vinegar by the Grey
```
Relational Analysis (GRA) method (Wang et al., 2014). The highest amounts of glu-
```
tamic acid are found in Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar, and of alanine in Shanxi aged
```
vinegar, Sichuan bran vinegar, and Shaanxi Qishan vinegar (Chen et al., 2013b; Li
```
```
et al., 2016b; Wang et al., 2016). Additionally, the first three brands of vinegar as well
```
as Tianjin Duliu mature vinegar contain a certain amount of small molecular weight
```
oligopeptides (< 1,000 Da), which accounts for 20–40% of the total protein con-
```
```
tent as analyzed by liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (Chen et al., 2009).
```
A previous study also showed that the total amount of amino acids in Baoning vin-
```
egar was the highest (3,438.55 mg/100 mL), followed by Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar
```
```
(1,682.36 mg/100 mL), Shanxi aged vinegar (1,346.54 mg/100 mL), and 3-year-old
```
```
Fujian Monascus vinegar (737.55 mg/100 mL), and the total amount of amino acids
```
```
increased during the ageing time (Zhang et al., 2014).
```
10.3.2.2 Organic Acids
As an acidic condiment, traditional vinegar involves a mass of organic acids, which
```
can be divided into volatile acids and non-volatile acids (Morales et al., 1998).
```
Volatile acids, about 90% of the total organic acids in traditional vinegar, constitute
the aroma core of the vinegar and range over formic acid, acetic acid, propanoic acid,
butanoic acid, 3-methylbutanoic acid, valeric acid, and hexanoic acid, with acetic
```
acid being the most abundant volatile acid (Sossou et al., 2009; Zhu et al., 2016). The
```
```
remaining percentage of total organic acids is non-volatile acids (e.g., lactic acid,
```
```
tartaric acid, citric acid, malic acid, succinic acid, and fumaric acid), which confer
```
soft acidity and flavorful taste in vinegar. Moreover, the content of organic acids will
change during the ageing process owing to the complex chemical reactions and water
177Vinegar Production in China
evaporation that take place. For example, the non-volatile acids accounted for 60% of
```
total acids in 8-year aged Shanxi vinegar (Chen et al., 2013b).
```
The organic acids in Chinese vinegar are mostly formed during the acetous fer-
```
mentation (AAF) process and the starter propagation process, by multiple metabolic
```
```
pathways of the cultivated microorganisms [e.g., lactic acid bacteria (LAB), acetic
```
acid bacteria, and yeasts], while a small part of the organic acids derives from the
```
raw material (Chen et al., 2013b; Qi et al., 2013; Xiao et al., 2011). The spontaneous
```
SSF results in higher amounts of non-volatile acids than the submerged fermentation,
which demonstrates that the brewing process has a vital impact on the composition
```
of organic acid in vinegar (Ho et al., 2017; Singhania et al., 2009). Furthermore, it
```
was reported that 32 different organic acids were detected in traditionally brewed
vinegar, compared to 29 in Shanxi aged vinegar, nine in Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar,
nine in Sichuan bran vinegar, eight in Shaanxi Qishan vinegar, and seven in Fujian
Monascus vinegar. Among them, seven common organic acids were detected in the
famous vinegars, i.e., oxalic, tartaric, pyruvic, lactic, acetic, citric, and succinic acid,
```
with lactic and acetic acids being the major sources of total acids (Nie et al., 2017;
```
```
Wu et al., 2017).
```
Different types of vinegar also contain different contents of organic acids
which obtain the special flavor, such as higher pyruvic and succinic acid contents
in Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar that confer to this vinegar acidic but not astringent
tastes. Additionally, higher citric and fumaric acid contents in Shanxi vinegar confer
soft sourness, while higher lactic acid content in Sichuan bran vinegar makes the
vinegar acidic yet somewhat sweet.
10.3.2.3 Minerals
Mineral substances in vinegar mainly originate from the water, the raw materials, as
well as the equipment and containers used during the brewing process. According
to previous reports, 40 kinds of inorganic elements were detected in the vinegar,
```
including 36 kinds of metal elements (e.g., K, Ca, Na, Mg, Mn, Zn, and Cu) and
```
```
four kinds of non-metallic elements (namely P, Se, B, and As) (Chen et al., 2009; Li
```
```
and Dai, 2015). Some studies described traditional vinegar containing more K, Ca,
```
Na, and Mg as alkaline food, despite the acidic taste. In Shanxi aged vinegar and
Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar, 38 mineral substances were determined by inductively
```
coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) and atomic emission spectrometry
```
```
(ICP-AES) (Zheng et al., 2012). The contents of 12 inorganic elements were signifi-
```
cantly different between Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar and Shanxi aged vinegar: the
contents of Cd, Ba, Mn, Zn, Ni, and Mo in Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar were higher
than those of Shanxi vinegar, while the contents of Al, Ca, Fe, Pb, Cs, and As were
lower than those in Shanxi vinegar. Among these, the higher Fe and Ca contents in
Shanxi aged vinegar can be explained by the fact that the water hardness in Shanxi
is generally higher than that in Zhenjiang.
10.3.2.4 Saccharides
The content of saccharides in traditional vinegar is mainly determined by total sugar
```
or reducing sugar analysis (Chen et al., 2013b). Although saccharides are mostly
```
fermented into acetic acid or other fermentation products, the residual content
178 Advances in Vinegar Production
remains in the end-product. The saccharides related with the flavor and density of
vinegar include glucose, maltose, mannose, arabinose, raffinose, and sorbose, which
derive from oligosaccharides contained in a variety of raw materials or from the
degradation of polysaccharides during the fermentation process. Glucose, lactose,
and sucrose were detected in brewed vinegars by the established vinegar nuclear
```
magnetic resonance (NMR) fingerprint technology, while higher lactose content in
```
```
Shanxi aged vinegar was exhibited compared with Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar (Li
```
```
et al., 2013).
```
10.3.2.5 Polyhydric Alcohols
Polyhydric alcohols, a type of alcohols containing two or more hydroxyl groups,
```
mainly consist of hexahydric alcohols (like sorbitol, mannitol, and maltitol), penta-
```
```
hydric alcohols (like xylitol and arabinitol), and tetrahydric alcohols (like erythritol),
```
which commonly have certain biological functions and are usually used as ingre-
```
dients for healthy foods (Zheng et al., 2010). Moreover, polyhydric alcohols have
```
significant impact on the flavor of vinegar. For example, erythritol, arabinitol, and
mannitol are associated with the sweetness of vinegars. Meanwhile, polyols within
vinegar are generally considered as geographical indicators of different vinegar-pro-
ducing regions. Erythritol, arabinitol, xylitol, inositol, mannitol, and sorbitol were
detected both in Shanxi vinegar and Zhenjiang vinegar by gas chromatograph–mass
```
spectrometry (GC–MS). However, the content of erythritol (221 mg/L) in Shanxi
```
aged vinegar was significantly higher than that of Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar
```
(73 mg/L), while the inositol and mannitol content in Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar
```
```
(343 mg/L and 359 mg/L, respectively) were significantly higher than in Shanxi aged
```
```
vinegar (251 mg/L and 224 mg/L, respectively) (Zheng et al., 2014).
```
10.3.2.6 Melanoidins
Melanoidins, a mixture of macromolecular compounds with complex structures and
different polymerization degrees, are brown substances derived from the Maillard
```
reaction between carbohydrates (generally sugars) and nitrogenous compounds with
```
```
free amino groups (such as amino acids, peptides, and proteins). Previous studies have
```
demonstrated that melanoidins have antioxidant, anti-bacterial, anti-tumor, and other
```
biological activities (Echavarría et al., 2012; Morales et al., 2012; Wen et al., 2018).
```
The smoking process of vinegar Pei was found to improve the antioxidant activ-
ity of Shanxi aged vinegar because of the generation of a large number of melanoi-
```
dins with various molecular weights (Zhang et al., 2016). Further study showed that
```
the antioxidant activity of melanoidins was relevant to free radical scavenging and
```
mitophagy (Yang et al., 2014). In addition, the melanoidin components in the vin-
```
egar, especially melanoidin with 3–5 kD molecular weight, had significant antibacte-
rial activity against Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Bacillus subtilis
```
owing to the metal ion chelation performance of melanoidins (Guo and Yang, 2016).
```
Lipid activity measurement results further indicated that melanoidin components
```
with 3–5 kD molecular weight performed the best lipid-lowering activity (Guo,
```
```
2015). Additionally, the antihypertensive properties of melanoidins in aged vinegar
```
```
were exhibited due to the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitory activity
```
```
in vitro (Lu, 2015; Mesías and Delgado-Andrade, 2017).
```
179Vinegar Production in China
10.3.2.7 Flavonoids
Flavonoids, a type of polyphenolic compound with 15 carbon atoms, have double
bonds, an aromatic ring, and other special structures. Flavonoids are the main anti-
oxidant active ingredients in traditional vinegars. It is considered that they are closely
related with the maintenance of physical well-being.
The comparison of total flavonoids in 26 different kinds of vinegar indicated
that the content of total flavonoids was quite different. Specifically, the content of
total flavonoids in Shanxi aged vinegar was 1.12–2.14 mg/mL and in Zhenjiang
```
aromatic vinegar was 1.22–2.03 mg/mL, followed by Beijing vinegar (1.37 mg/mL)
```
```
and Shanghai balsamic vinegar (1.51 mg/mL) (Xu et al., 2006). An amount of
```
3.03 mg/mL of total flavonoids was determined in 5-year Shanxi aged vinegar by
```
Zhai et al. (2015).
```
There is a dearth of information on the structure of flavonoid components in vin-
egar. Only one type of flavonoids, catechin, was detected in Japanese brown rice
```
vinegar by high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) based on reference
```
```
substances (20 kinds of flavonoids, such as rutin, luteolin, quercetin, and isorham-
```
```
netin) and retention times (Chou et al., 2015). The new national standard for Shanxi
```
aged vinegar has added the determination of total flavonoids. However, due to the
unclear structure of the flavonoid components, a more specific HPLC assay is dif-
ficult to establish and the structure of the flavonoid components in vinegar needs to
be further studied.
10.3.2.8 Tetramethylpyrazine
Tetramethylpyrazine, or ligustrazine, is one of the main active ingredients of
Ligusticum chuanxiong Hort, a traditional Chinese medicinal plant used to treat
```
various diseases including cardiovascular functions (Zhao et al., 2010). However,
```
the mechanism of the formation of tetramethylpyrazine in vinegar is not clear. It
is generally believed that the generation of tetramethylpyrazine in vinegar results
from the Maillard reaction. The proposed mechanism is that the Strecker degrada-
tion reduced ketone or deoxygenated ketone in the later stage of Maillard reaction
may result in the generation of tetramethylpyrazine. Another hypothesis is that the
acetoin produced by the amino acids and sugar in the vinegar combines with ammo-
nia to generate an intermediate product, which will then be condensed with acetoin
```
to form tetramethylpyrazine (Chen et al., 2013a).
```
At present, the tetramethylpyrazine in vinegar is mostly detected in Shanxi
aged vinegar, Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar, and Sichuan Baoning vinegar but not
```
in white vinegar and white rice vinegar (Song et al., 2014). Chen et al. (2013a)
```
reported that the content of tetramethylpyrazine ranged from ~0.02 mg/kg to
131.1 mg/kg in 36 vinegar samples nationwide, and the higher content was found
in Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar and Shanxi aged vinegar, indicating that tetra-
methylpyrazine varies greatly among the different types of vinegar. Among
them, in Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar it was found in the range 4.60–131.1 mg/L.
In addition, the content of tetramethylpyrazine in the Shanxi aged vinegar with
```
geographical indication (GI) ranged from 10.2 to 88.7 mg/L, and the aver-
```
```
age was significantly higher than the non-GIs and other control vinegars (Song
```
```
et al., 2014).
```
180 Advances in Vinegar Production
10.3.2.9 Volatile Substances
The volatile substances of vinegar are mainly generated in the process of alcoholic
fermentation and AAF and include esters, alcohols, aldehydes, phenols and phe-
nolic acids, ketones, and heterocyclic compounds, as discussed in more detail in
other chapters of this book. These compounds endow vinegar with its special flavor,
although they only account for a small proportion of the vinegar components.
Esters with fruity or floral aromas are abundant in well-known Chinese vinegars,
```
such as ethyl acetate in Shanxi aged vinegar (64.8 mg/L) (Lv, 2008). In the complex
```
fermentation system, the esters are formed by the integration of organic acids and
alcohols under the catalysis of esterase. Among the esters, ethyl acetate and ethyl
lactate are predominant in vinegar, while ethyl succinate, isoamyl acetate, propyl
acetate, isoamyl hexanoate, methyl hexanoate, butyl acetate, and ethyl isovalerate
are contained in trace amounts.
Ethanol is typically the main product of sugar substrates fermentation by yeasts
and is produced during the pre-stage of AAF. It is a common ingredient in various
```
types of vinegar; in fact, it is still the most abundant alcohol in vinegar although it
```
is largely oxidized to acetic acid and undergoes esterification reactions with acids
during the fermentation stage. Besides ethanol, alcohols also include methanol,
β-phenethyl alcohol, isoamyl alcohol, 2,3-butanediol, propanol, isopropanol, isobu-
tyl alcohol, and so on. Some of them may impart unpleasant odors, and excessive
levels of higher alcohols might produce bitter sensations.
Aldehydes in vinegar are produced by microbial fermentation or by the degrada-
tion of amino acids, which has a certain impact on the quality of vinegar. Aldehydes
detected in vinegar mainly include acetaldehyde, 3-methylbutyraldehyde, vanillin,
furfural, glyceraldehyde, and phenylacetaldehyde. Furfural is generated by the heat-
ing of pentoses, and the vinegar brewing technology that adopts the smoked process
displays a higher content of furfural. Trace amounts of acetaldehyde play a role in
```
the harmony of flavors; however, excessive amounts of aldehydes result in a nega-
```
tive impact on the quality of vinegar, mainly as heavy spicy flavors and irritative
sensations.
Phenols and phenolic acids normally appear in plant tissues combined with mac-
romolecular compounds. Traditional vinegar also contains certain amounts of phe-
nolic acids deriving from the decomposition of raw materials by microbes during
the vinegar fermentation processes. These trace phenolic acids and phenols include
eugenol, vanillic acid, salicylic acid, and 4-ethyl guaiacol, which have low threshold
values highly affecting the essential aroma of vinegar with soft and pleasant notes.
Ketones are generally produced by thermal oxidative degradation, amino acid
degradation, or microbial oxidation of unsaturated fatty acids. They emit sweet
```
floral and fruity aromas, mainly the methyl ketones (C3 -C17 ) which confer unique
```
aromas to vinegar, especially the longer chain ketones. Moreover, small amounts
```
of 3-hydroxybutanone as well as 2,3-butanedione (or diacetyl; aroma threshold 0.2
```
```
mg/L) confer a pleasant honey-like sweet aroma; however, excessive amounts bring
```
unpleasant flavors to vinegar.
Heterocyclic compounds in vinegar are primarily produced by microbial fermen-
tation and can also be produced by Strecker degradation and Maillard reactions,
which typically have nutty, charred, and toasted flavors. So far, the main vinegar
181Vinegar Production in China
heterocyclic compounds which have been identified include pyrazine compounds
and furans. Their types and proportions are directly related to the aroma type and
elegance of vinegar.
In a recent study, a total of 360 volatile compounds were identified in Zhenjiang
```
aromatic vinegar (Zhou et al., 2017). The flavor of vinegar is a complex blend of
```
volatile compounds that are intertwined to confer the vinegar its unique aroma. The
diversity of microbial metabolites highly contributes to the flavor and aroma of the
vinegar products, and a comprehensive understanding of the involved fermentation
microorganisms is a prerequisite for selecting strains for culture implementation.
10.3.3 funCtional properties of CHinese Vinegar
Health promoting and therapeutic properties of vinegar, such as antimicrobial, anti-
fatigue, antioxidant, and antihypertensive activities, have been traditionally acknowl-
```
edged for the prevention of negative health effects (Budak et al., 2014; Petsiou et al.,
```
```
2014). Historically, Chinese medicine books have recorded the medical role of vin-
```
egar. For example, 17 prescriptions with cereal vinegar to treat burns, hernia, ring-
worm, and 11 types of viruses have been recorded in the ancient book Fifty-Two
```
Diseases unearthed in 1973 (Chen et al., 2016). A famous doctor, Hua Tuo, used
```
garlic and vinegar to cure a serious case of roundworm infection and established a
precedent of diet therapy for emergency treatment. Moreover, consumption of vin-
egar is advocated to improve the immune system and maintain the blood acid–base
balance. Specifically, the functional properties of vinegars are as follows.
10.3.3.1 Antimicrobial Function
Vinegar has strong antimicrobial properties, which makes it suitable for substantive
applications. In a certain concentration, vinegar has the ability to destroy respiratory
pathogens, such as Pneumococcus, Micrococcus catarrhalis, Diplococcus pneu-
```
moniae, alpha Streptococcus, and flu bacteria (Xin et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2003). The
```
concentration of hydrogen ions reaching 5–6% in a vinegar solution is sufficient to con-
```
trol the growth of cold viruses (Xu et al., 2003). Studies have also shown that vinegar
```
with a concentration of 0.1% acetic acid has bacteriostatic or bactericidal effect on food-
borne pathogens, including E. coli O157:H7, Salmonella enteritidis, S. typhimurium,
```
Vibrio parahaemolyticus, and S. aureus (Chang and Fang, 2007; Entani et al., 1997;
```
```
Entani et al., 1998; Medina et al., 2007; Sengun and Karapinar, 2004).
```
In addition, consumers typically prefer safe methods for inhibiting or eradicat-
ing foodborne pathogenic microorganisms in food. Vinegar as a natural disinfec-
tant was found effective in eliminating pathogenic bacteria on fresh vegetables by
```
soaking them in vinegar for a certain period of time (Chang and Fang, 2007). The
```
```
plausible explanation may be that entry of the organic acids within vinegar (mainly
```
```
acetic acid) into cell membranes of microorganisms leads to bacterial cell fatality.
```
Additionally, several factors, including the type of bacterial strains, temperature,
pH, acetic acid concentration, and ionic strength, also influence the antimicrobial
efficiency of the organic acids.
Acetic acid was specifically recognized as the most fatal acid against E. coli
```
O157:H7 (a foodborne pathogen), followed by lactic, citric, and malic acids
```
182 Advances in Vinegar Production
```
(Budak et al., 2014; Ryu et al., 1999). Furthermore, a higher antibacterial effect
```
of vinegar was exhibited compared to that of acetic acid and other organic acids
diluted separately. Finally, acid-endurance of Aspergillus niger could be markedly
suppressed in vinegar containing 0.2% acetic acid, while the acidity of other organic
acids was as high as 0.6%.
10.3.3.2 Antifatigue Function
The modern medical research has confirmed that vinegar can relieve physical
fatigue. After ingesting organic acids such as acetic acid in vinegar, the lactic acid
and pyruvic acid in human body that cause muscle fatigue could be decomposed
by the tricarboxylic acid cycle to relieve fatigue. One report showed that Zhenjiang
aromatic vinegar capsules at the dosage of 600 mg/kg b.w./d allayed tiredness of
```
mice (Lu and Zhou, 2002). Another animal study demonstrated that the swimming
```
time of mice fed mulberry vinegar was significantly higher than the control group,
indicating that the vinegar to some extent possessed antifatigue abilities for mice
```
(Zhang et al., 2007).
```
10.3.3.3 Antioxidant Function
Under normal physiological conditions, the generation and elimination of reactive
```
oxygen species (ROS) in the organism are maintained in a relatively balanced state.
```
However, a large number of intracellular ROS cannot be cleared in time thus result-
```
ing in oxidative stress (Rodriguez and Redman, 2005). Oxidative substances, such
```
as superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radical, accumulate in the body and
```
directly or indirectly induce the damage of cell components (e.g., gene mutations,
```
```
protein denaturation, and lipid peroxidation). These damages accelerate body age-
```
ing and induce a series of diseases like atherosclerosis, liver damage, and tumors
```
(Buonocore et al., 2010; Maes et al., 2011). The significant antioxidant activity of
```
polyphenols, flavonoids, melanoidins, and other natural bioactive substances in vin-
egar can maintain the body’s oxidation balance and reduce incidences of chronic and
```
degenerative illnesses (Davalos et al., 2005; Fernandez-Mar et al., 2012; Ramadan
```
```
and Al-Ghamdi, 2012).
```
In recent years, extensive in vitro and in vivo experiments have exhibited the anti-
oxidant capacity of grain or fruit vinegars. For example, in vitro studies showed that
```
the antioxidant capacity of Shanxi aged vinegar is 0.1% vitamin C equivalent (Chen
```
```
et al., 2016). In vivo studies reported that traditional Chinese vinegars could inhibit
```
the oxidation of cholesterol and unsaturated fatty acids to reduce the deposition of
cholesterol and its oxide on the artery walls and promote the metabolism of unsatu-
rated fatty acids, demonstrating that they can play a preventive role in cardiovascular
```
diseases (Chen et al., 2016; Xia et al., 2017).
```
The traditional Shaanxi Qishan vinegar was found to possess higher 2,2-diphe-
```
nyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH) radical-scavenging activity (an important index widely
```
```
used to evaluate the antioxidant capacity of samples) compared to Zhenjiang aro-
```
```
matic vinegar, Sichuan Baoning vinegar, and Shanxi aged vinegar (Feng, 2009).
```
```
Moreover, the total cholesterol (TC), triglyceride (TG), and arteriosclerosis index
```
of mice that received Shaanxi Qishan vinegar were lower than those of the control
group, indicating that this vinegar has a significant hypolipidemic effect.
183Vinegar Production in China
The DPPH radical-scavenging activity of cereal vinegars is generally higher than
fruit vinegars, which may be attributed to the higher total phenolic content and fla-
vanols present in cereal vinegars, while among cereal vinegars Shanxi aged vinegar
```
showed higher radical scavenging activity than Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar (in less
```
```
than 3 months of ageing and without smoked process in Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar).
```
Kiwifruit vinegar exhibited the highest scavenging activity among fruit vinegars
```
(Ren et al., 2017). Previous studies have also demonstrated that kiwifruit has higher
```
```
levels of phenolic contents than persimmon and apple (Du, 2009).
```
```
Xu et al. (2005) showed that Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar had an inhibitory
```
```
effect on Cu 2+ -induced oxidative modification of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) and
```
blocked the oxidation of modified LDL. Furthermore, the 1% freeze-dried powder
of Shanxi aged vinegar resulted in a significant reduction of TG, TC, and LDL in
```
hyperlipidemic mice, exerting its hypolipidemic and antioxidation action (Liu and
```
```
Yang, 2015). The antidiabetic effect of Chinese white rice vinegar and bitter buck-
```
wheat vinegar on blood glucose control in streptozotocin-induced diabetic rats has
```
also been reported (Gu et al., 2012; Ma, 2010; Wang et al., 2012).
```
```
A study by Qiu et al. (2010) reported that the activities of the antioxidant enzymes
```
```
superoxide dismutase (SOD) and glutathione peroxidases were significantly
```
increased in the liver tissue and serum of mice fed traditional oat vinegar, indicating
strong antioxidant activity of the vinegar on mice with impaired livers. Xiang et al.
```
(2012) and Du et al. (2012) reported that Hovenia dulcis fermented vinegar could
```
protect the livers of alcoholic mice by reducing TG and TC content in the serum and
liver tissue, as well as the level of malondialdehyde in liver cells. The results showed
that the vinegar could reduce the side effects of alcohol and had a certain protective
effect on liver of ethanol-induced injury.
High ROS levels can damage DNA and DNA repair related enzymes and acti-
vate protooncogenes, resulting in abnormity of intracellular signaling molecules and
```
their regulatory factors and even in cancerous cells (Gorrini et al., 2013). Traditional
```
vinegar containing natural bioactive substances can prevent and inhibit the occur-
rence of the tumor by inducing tumor cell differentiation and inhibiting tumor cell
```
proliferation (Wang et al., 2008). Moreover, the ethyl acetate in Shanxi aged vinegar
```
```
(0.01%) significantly inhibited the proliferation of cancer cells in vitro, demonstrat-
```
```
ing the anticancer function of this vinegar (Chen and Gullo, 2015).
```
10.3.3.4 Antihypertensive Function
Vinegar can promote sodium excretion from the human body and improve the abnor-
mal metabolism of sodium to inhibit the rise of blood pressure caused by excess salt.
In China, traditionally vinegar-soaked peanuts or vinegar-soaked soybean have been
used to control hypertension for a long time. The mechanism of hypertension is
related with the renin-angiotensin system and the nervous system, in which angio-
tensin is closely associated with ACE. Studies have explored the effect of vinegar
on lowering blood pressure, which has been verified in hypertensive rats. Rice vin-
egar was also found to be able to inhibit ACE activity and reduce blood pressure in
```
vitro (Kondo et al., 2001). In addition to reducing blood pressure, vinegar shows a
```
```
decrease in rennin activity upon the ingestion of acetic acid; therefore, consumption
```
of vinegar could reduce plasma renin activity as well as blood pressure.
184 Advances in Vinegar Production
10.3.4 quality Control and eValuation of CHinese Vinegar
Since the quality of vinegar, which is popularly consumed as condiment, can directly
affect human health, Chinese governments have paid more attention to the qual-
```
ity control of traditional vinegar (Zhang et al., 2006). The China State Bureau of
```
Quality and Technical Supervision issued the market allowance policy on vinegar
quality and safety in 2002 and revised some items in 2016. In national hygiene stan-
dards for Chinese vinegar based on the overall quality of most products, the con-
```
tents of free mineral acids, arsenic (As), lead (Pb), aflatoxin B1, and the number of
```
```
total plate counts, coliforms, and pathogens (Salmonella spp., Shigella spp., and S.
```
```
aureus) are strictly limited. Besides, the China State Bureau of Standards has issued
```
the related standards to specify the technical requirements, test methods, inspection
rules, and requirements for labeling, packaging, transporting, and storage, to guar-
```
antee the quality of vinegar and public health (Figure 10.1).
```
With regard to sensory evaluation, it requires a panel of sophisticated experts
and a limited number of vinegar samples examined per tasting session, in order to
```
accurately describe items or take decisions (Tesfaye et al., 2002). Today sensory
```
evaluation still provides a key technique for the food industry, especially the brew-
ing industry, due to the superb sensitivity and discrimination ability of the chemi-
```
cal senses (Zhang et al., 2008). However, various chemical analysis methods, such
```
as GC, GC–MS, and electronic nose, have been developed to determine the vin-
egar compounds and control vinegar quality, since accuracy and objectivity cannot
always be ensured in vinegar sensory evaluations due to the influence of the asses-
```
sors’ health conditions and emotions and the effect of the environment (Cocchi et al.,
```
```
2004; Giordano et al., 2003; Zhang et al., 2008).
```
```
Physicochemical indexes, namely the total acids content (TAC), non-vola-
```
```
tile acids content (NVAC), and soluble salt-free solids content (SSFSC), three
```
FIGURE 10.1 The standards of fermented vinegar quality in China.
185Vinegar Production in China
important quality indicators, have a significant influence on the quality assess-
ment of Chinese vinegar. In general, the higher content of the three indicators in
vinegar means a better quality. The TAC and NVAC affect the taste of vinegar,
and the SSFSC is an important indicator of Chinese vinegar flavor and nutri-
```
tional value, as it is the reflection of soluble solids (without water and salt) con-
```
tained in the vinegar including sugars, free amino acids, protein, and other minor
components.
Furthermore, Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar, Shanxi aged vinegar, Tianjin Duliu
mature vinegar, and Fujian Monascus vinegar have applied the national stan-
dard of GI products, grading the vinegar based on the physicochemical indexes
```
(Table 10.2).
```
10.4 PRODUCTION TECHNOLOGIES OF CHINESE VINEGAR
As early as 1058 BC, a book named Rites of Zhou in China gave a brief account of
```
vinegar brewing. It was verified that Taiyuan (a city of Shanxi Province) had a cer-
```
tain size and number of vinegar brewing workshops in 479 BC. Moreover, in the 5th
century AD the famous Chinese agricultural scientist Sixie Jia made clear descrip-
tion of vinegar production technology and its principles and 23 different methods
for brewing vinegars in his book Qi Min Yao Shu. Between 369 and 404 AD, the
Chinese techniques for making rice vinegar were introduced to Japan. Furthermore,
during the Ming and Qing dynasties, the development of Chinese vinegar production
technology reached a climax, and a well-known vineyard specializing in the produc-
tion of court vinegar was created in Taiyuan. Based on predecessors’ experiences,
the vinegar brewing approaches of intense vaporization in summer, removal of ice
in winter, and an extra progress of “smoked vinegar” were adapted to enhance the
sourness, color, and flavor of vinegar. In addition, local best sorghum as raw mate-
rial was introduced to produce aged vinegar, and a set of sorghum vinegar methods
were summed.
In vinegar brewing biochemical reactions take place, by which acetic acid bac-
```
teria (AAB) convert sugars and other substances into acetic acid. The presence of
```
AAB as well as the suitable conditions for AAB proliferation and fermentation are
two indispensable prerequisites for vinegar production. Over the ages, people all
over China have created a variety of local characteristics of the vinegar process.
Chinese cereal vinegars are brewed either by SSF processes or by liquid-state
```
fermentation (LSF) processes (submerged) (Liu et al., 2004). Unlike European
```
vinegars fermented by pure-culture LSF process, the brewing of Chinese tradi-
tional vinegar generally adopts spontaneous SSF involving multiple microbial
species. These rich cultures generate a plethora of enzymes and metabolites in
the solid substrates, which resemble the natural habitat of these microorganisms
during the SSF process.
In recent decades, the research on LSF has progressed rapidly and most large
enterprises adopt this technology to meet the needs of the modern large-scale
production and to improve the vinegar production efficiency. Moreover, the AAF
process of fruit vinegars is usually carried out by LSF or semi-SSF by inoculating
```
selected AAB strains (Solieri and Giudici, 2009).
```

187Vinegar Production in China
10.4.1 solid -state fermentation of CHinese Vinegar
SSF has been defined as the process in which the growth and metabolism of the
microorganisms take place on solid substrates lacking or nearly lacking free water
```
but with enough moisture to support the fermentation (Singhania et al., 2009). SSF
```
has been widely used to produce vinegar since ancient times in China. This type of
vinegar fermentation is based on grain-based raw materials and complicated, multi-
```
strain metabolism (Wang et al., 2016).
```
10.4.1.1 The Basic Technology of SSF
Vinegar brewing is a complex biochemical process that involves starch sacchari-
fication, alcoholic fermentation, and AAF, as well as protein degradation and fla-
```
vor ingredients formation (Lu et al., 2018). In general, the traditional SSF process
```
involves steaming of starch raw materials, mixing of bran and rice husk, addition
```
of “Qu” (a starter) and other additives, and adjustment of the moisture of the fer-
```
mentation substrates. Moreover, additional enzyme preparations are not used in the
traditional SSF, since the enzymes and microorganisms required are provided from
the Qu and the environment. The fermented mash is mixed with bran and other fill-
ers to bring it to the suitable solid state. In addition, most vinegar factories do not
supplement AAB in the vinegar Pei and still apply the natural AAF. However, some
manufacturers stir in a certain amount of ripe fresh vinegar as “seed” to speed up the
AAF without losing the consistency of vinegar flavor.
Qu, a cereal starter of traditional Chinese vinegar, consists of multitype microbes
```
and enzyme systems (Brandt, 2014). It is an important saccharifying and fermenta-
```
tion agent that is widely used to accelerate and steer the traditional vinegar brewing
```
process (Li et al., 2015b). There are various types of Qu in China, namely “Daqu,”
```
“Xiaoqu,” “Fuqu,” “Hongqu,” and “Maiqu.”
Daqu is also prepared by an ancient SSF technology and is based on a single wheat
or mixed wheat, barley, and pea as raw material. The Daqu fermentation process
```
mainly involves three steps: (1) material crushing, mixing, and brick molding, (2)
```
```
spontaneous SSF with controlled temperature, and (3) drying and ripening (Li et al.,
```
```
2017). Also, the matured Daqu mainly includes Rhizopus, Aspergillus, yeast, and
```
LAB. Despite the long production period, this starter results in a tasty vinegar and is
still adopted in the production of Shanxi vinegar and other famous vinegars to date.
Xiaoqu, a grainy starter, is prepared using ground rice, rice hull, or wheat bran,
adding or not some Chinese medicinal herbs and inoculating molds at the appropri-
ate temperature and humidity conditions. The dominating microbes in Xiaoqu are
Rhizopus, Mucor, and yeast to provide saccharifying power.
Fuqu is based on wheat bran as the main raw material, and Aspergillus is inocu-
lated as pure culture. This starter, with economic cost and strong saccharifying power,
can shorten the production cycle and is universally applied to initiate cereal vinegars.
Hongqu also has a strong saccharifying capacity and is made from rice as solid-
state medium and inoculated with Monascus. It is widely used in the brewing of
Monascus vinegar and rose vinegar.
Broken wheat is the culture medium of Maiqu that possesses two main enzymes,
protease and amylase. Aspergillus oryzae, Rhizopus, and yeast are enriched in Maiqu.
188 Advances in Vinegar Production
During the SSF process, the temperature management is pivotal for vinegar
production since temperature has a crucial impact on the microbial consortia and
```
the functional enzymes (Liu et al., 2004; Yao et al., 2006). Generally, the vinegar
```
Pei is deposited into the pot or pool at a low temperature to slow the growth of
contaminating bacteria, maintain the activity of amylase and yeast, and inhibit
the spoilage of vinegar Pei. The initial temperature control for putting vinegar
```
Pei into the pot is based on two factors: (1) the starch concentration (higher con-
```
```
centration of starch requires lower initial temperature), and (2) the climatic condi-
```
```
tions (the initial temperature of vinegar Pei is preferably not lower than 24°C in
```
```
winter or higher than 28°C in summer). Furthermore, the temperature in the pot
```
should be controlled in the range of 38–46°C by pressing and turning over the
vinegar Pei to decrease the rate of ethanol consumption and reduce oxygen supply
```
and heat production in the AAF step (Li et al., 2015c). Besides, the quintessential
```
fermentation temperature curve presents an ascent at first and a descent later dur-
ing the AAF process.
10.4.1.2 The Fermentation Features of SSF
SSF is considered a more suitable and useful technique for the production of tra-
ditional vinegar, due to its low energy requirements, simplicity, generation of little
wastewater effluent, and good product characteristics in a smaller reactor volume
```
(Singhania et al., 2009; Yao et al., 2006). Important fermentation features of SSF
```
vinegar are:
```
(1) The diversity of raw materials and plethora of nutrients. The main materi-
```
als for vinegar SSF are widely available and various in kind. Meanwhile,
the many available auxiliary materials equip the vinegar fermentation with
complete nutrient substrate composition. These raw materials are not only
beneficial to the growth of microorganisms, but also make the reaction
substrates effective regarding acetic acid, flavor, and color generation and
consistency. The time needed for completion of the SSF process is obvi-
```
ously longer than that of LSF; therefore, the brewed vinegar from SSF has
```
enhanced flavors due to alcohols and esters formation, deep amber or red-
dish-brown color, and good clarity state. Moreover, this vinegar is rich in
amino acids and non-volatile acids that make the vinegar taste soft-sour
despite the high acetic acid content. Besides, noticeably higher SSFSC is
exhibited in the traditional SSF vinegar compared to other vinegars. These
excellent qualities make traditional SSF vinegar production technology
uniquely advantageous.
```
(2) The coexistence of multiple fermentation microbes and enzymes. The vin-
```
egar production system of SSF in an open fermentation mode, in which
AAB, molds, yeasts, and other microorganisms, as well as enzymes,
coexist, is complex and changeable. The functional enzymes include
liquefied amylase, glucoamylase, alcohol enzyme, protease, cellulase,
pectinase, and other enzymes co-acting for starch saccharification, gen-
```
eration of alcohol, AAF, and other reactions (Huang et al., 2017). The syn-
```
ergism of these microbes and enzymes in the SSF process not only plays
189Vinegar Production in China
a key role in the formation of color, flavor, and body of vinegar but also
lays a good foundation for the acquisition of outstanding end-products
```
(Zhao and Li, 2005).
```
```
(3) Multiplicate Qu making technology. Vinegar Qu is the starter of traditional
```
SSF vinegar. Although the types and origins of the raw materials and the
methods used to produce vinegar are different, the production of these vin-
egars has similar principles and scientific bases. That is, the specific micro-
biotas have been well enriched and retained with the unique ecological
```
environments (discrepant climatic conditions such as temperature, humid-
```
```
ity, and light in different regions) and manufacturing procedures, through
```
```
long time repeated practices of Qu preparation (Li et al., 2016a). These
```
microorganisms grow, multiply, and metabolize under appropriate condi-
tions during the vinegar brewing process to produce multitype enzymes
functional for vinegar fermentation. Through the traditional multi-strain,
mixed fermentation method, the end-product is of superb quality in all
```
aspects (color, smell, and taste).
```
Nevertheless, there are some disadvantages associated with the SSF process for vin-
egar production, such as poor heat transfer, difficult control of the process param-
eters, and intensive labor. Therefore, industries have combined this technology with
modern industrialization and mechanization to overcome these drawbacks.
10.4.1.3 The Microflora of SSF
With the development of microbial ecology techniques, an increasing number of
works have investigated the microbial dynamics and communities during traditional
```
Chinese vinegar fermentation (Bevilacqua et al., 2016; Li et al., 2015b; Wang et al.,
```
```
2015; Zhang et al., 2017). These studies provide crucial information about the roles
```
and function of the microbial consortia in traditional vinegar. Microbial popula-
tions involved in the SSF processing of various resources, such as non-autoclaved
```
cereals (Bevilacqua et al., 2016), Qu (Li et al., 2015b), vinegar Pei starter (Wang et
```
```
al., 2015), and the open process environment, illustrate the diversity of the cereal
```
```
vinegar microbiota (Li et al., 2016a).
```
Many culture-dependent approaches have been used to characterize patterns of
microbial community diversity in the SSF process of cereal vinegars and have iso-
```
lated strains, including LAB (Lactobacillus and Pediococcus), AAB (Acetobacter,
```
```
Gluconobacter, and Gluconacetobacter), and Bacillus spp., which are the main gen-
```
```
era easily isolated during cereal vinegar fermentation (Li et al., 2015c; Wu et al.,
```
```
2010; Wu et al., 2012a; Wu et al., 2012b). Moreover, Acetobacter and Lactobacillus
```
```
are acknowledged as functional microbes for vinegar production (Nie et al., 2013;
```
```
Wu et al., 2012a).
```
Recent applications of culture-independent approaches such as PCR-denaturing
```
gradient gel electrophoresis (DGGE) and amplicon-based high-throughput sequenc-
```
ing analysis have provided a blueprint of microbial diversity in the vinegar eco-
systems for Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar, Shanxi aged vinegar, Sichuan Baoning
```
vinegar, Shaanxi Qishan vinegar, and Tianjin Duliu mature vinegar (Li et al., 2016b;
```
```
Nie et al., 2015; Peng et al., 2015; Wang et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2017).
```
190 Advances in Vinegar Production
For example, a 951 genera-containing picture of the microbial diversity in vinegar
```
Pei of Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar was revealed by metagenomic sequencing (Wu
```
```
et al., 2017). AAF, a dynamic and intricate process, can be divided into distinguish-
```
```
ing stages. Wang et al. (2016) have reported that obvious differences in the patterns
```
of community assembly occurred at different AAF stages of Zhenjiang aromatic
vinegar production. Specifically, Lactobacillus was predominant in the early stage
of AAF, while Acetobacter, Lactococcus, Gluconacetobacter, Enterococcus, and
```
Bacillus were prevalent in the later stage of AAF (Wang et al., 2016). At the species
```
level, Lactobacillus in this vinegar Pei was represented by 19 species , in which
L. helveticus, L. hatiateri, L. pontis, and L. panis accounted for 74, 17, 7.7, and 1.1%,
respectively. The proportion of other LAB species was less than 0.5%. A study con-
firmed that L. helveticus was a probiotic bacterium that possessed strong proteolytic
ability and could produce various amino acids, bioactive peptides, and other func-
```
tional active substances (Ong and Shah, 2008).
```
In AAB, nine Acetobacter members and six Gluconacetobacter affiliations were
detected in Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar. A. pasteurianus accounted for the largest
```
proportion in Acetobacter (about 93%), followed by A. syzygii (4.0%), and the per-
```
centage of G. intermedius was 1.21% in Gluconobacter. As for fungi, Aspergillus
existed in the whole AAF process, and a total of 21 yeast genera were identified in
vinegar Pei, such as Cryptococcus, Debaryomyces, Candida, and Saccharomyces.
Furthermore, correlation analysis based on the bidirectional orthogonal partial
```
least squares (O2PLS) model revealed the relationships between the succession
```
of microbiota and flavor dynamics. The results showed that seven genera includ-
ing Acetobacter, Lactobacillus, Enhydrobacter, Lactococcus, Gluconacetobacer,
Bacillus, and Staphylococcus during AAF of Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar all con-
tributed to the change of volatile flavors, in which Acetobacter and Staphylococcus
```
were mainly responsible for the change of amino acids (Wang et al., 2016).
```
During the Shanxi aged vinegar fermentation process, higher microbial diver-
sity was exhibited in Daqu compared with alcoholic fermentation and AAF samples
```
(Nie et al., 2015; Nie et al., 2017). The bacterial and fungal community of Daqu at the
```
genus level contained Saccharopolyspora, Staphylococcus, Bacillus, Lactobacillus,
and Weissella, and Saccharomycopsis, Pichia, Eurotium, and Monascus, respec-
tively. Once alcoholic fermentation commenced, the microbial assembly dis-
tinctly changed, and the microbial diversity gradually decreased during this stage.
Lactobacillus, Weissella, Saccharomyces, Saccharomycopsis, and Aspergillus were
the dominant genera during alcoholic fermentation, especially Saccharomyces cere-
visiae, which was the dominant alcohol-producing yeast at this step. The number of
genera increased in the initial AAF process, but a great deal of microbes disappeared
as AAF progressed. Additionally, AAB and LAB were the two dominant bacterial
groups and played important roles in AAF. Although Klebsiella and Escherichia
were detected during AAF of Shanxi aged vinegar and their functional roles remain
unclear, these bacteria are possibly related to the vinegar flavor. Saccharomycopsis
fibuligera was the only fungus that existed during the whole fermentation process.
The use of different herb Daqu changed the bacterial community of Sichuan
```
Baoning vinegar Pei in lab scale (Zhang et al., 2017). However, the presence of two
```
dominant AAB and LAB was displayed. Apart from the two dominant bacteria,
191Vinegar Production in China
```
Bacillus and Oceanobacillus (with the capability of biosynthesizing acetoin) pre-
```
dominated in vinegar Pei. Unlike Shanxi aged vinegar and Zhenjiang aromatic vin-
egar Pei, Pichia, Geotrichum, and Trichoderma were the dominant fungi in bran
vinegar Pei, which demonstrated that differences in the raw materials, Daqu, and
fermentation methods could lead to variations of the dominant microbes.
```
During the whole Daqu fermentation process (used for the startup of Shaanxi Qishan
```
```
vinegar fermentation), the phylotypes of Enterobacteriales and Lactobacillales as
```
well as Saccharomycetales and Eurotiales were the dominating bacteria and fungi,
```
respectively (Gan et al., 2017; Li et al., 2015a). Besides, the bacterial phylotypes of
```
Bacillales and fungal phylotypes of Mucorales were also the ultimate survivors in
Qishan Daqu. Furthermore, the microbial communities in Qishan Daqu tended to
evolve a thermotolerant and drought-resistant community structure during the SSF
```
process (Li et al., 2016a).
```
The orders of Lactobacillales and Rhodospirillales were the most prevalent bac-
terial communities during the Shaanxi vinegar AAF process, influencing the flavor
```
and taste of this vinegar (Li et al., 2016b). However, Enterobacteriales and Bacillales
```
were only involved in the initial AAF process. In addition, the biomass of total bac-
teria in the mid-term AAF process was much higher than that in the initial and final
AAF stages. Overall, the bacterial phylotypes of Acetobacter, Lactobacillus, and
Pseudomonas were retained in the final vinegar Pei.
For the SSF process of Tianjin Duliu mature vinegar, the dominant bacte-
rial genera in the Duliu-Daqu were Weissella, Lactobacillus, Lactococcus, and
```
Streptomyces, among which Streptomyces (e.g., S. rangoonensis, S. cacaoi, S. gib-
```
```
sonii, S. radiopugnans, and S. albus) was highly abundant (Nie et al., 2013; Peng et
```
```
al., 2015). As distinct from Shanxi-Daqu, AAB were not found, and the fungal gen-
```
era of Saccharomycopsis and Pichia were relatively fewer in Duliu-Daqu. During
the AAF process, the total abundance of Lactobacillus, Nostoc, Acetobacter, and
Gluconacetobacter was about 95%, and the relative abundance of the three genera
except Lactobacillus was enhanced as the fermentation proceeded, indicating that
they were dominant functional microorganisms for vinegar fermentation. The spe-
cies richness of LAB gradually decreased through the AAF process, but the relative
abundance of LAB was higher than other bacteria, and Lactobacillus acetotolerans
and L. helveticus existed during the entire AAF. Unlike the bacterial community in
Daqu, Lactococcus and Streptomyces were not detected in the vinegar Pei samples.
10.4.1.4 The Representative Vinegars of SSF
In China, there are more than 20 types of homemade vinegar on the market, and
each type of vinegar with specific local features has its own taste and flavor. They are
mostly produced by a typical aerobic SSF technique. The famous traditional Chinese
vinegars, Shanxi aged vinegar, Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar, and Sichuan bran vin-
```
egar, are the representative products of this technique (Chen et al., 2013b; Nie et al.,
```
```
2015; Xu et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2017).
```
Shanxi aged vinegar is the most famous and representative vinegar in the north of
China, and the best-known Shanxi vinegar is produced in Qingxu County of Taiyuan.
```
Its brewing methods adopt high-quality sorghum as the main raw material (mix-
```
```
ing numerous Daqus), low-temperature alcoholic fermentation, high-temperature
```
192 Advances in Vinegar Production
```
expeditious acetification, moderate-temperature roasting (smoking), and long-term
```
```
ageing involving exposure in the sun in open containers (insolating) during the sum-
```
mer and removing the ice that forms during winter in order to increase density, bal-
```
ance flavor, and increase color and luster (Figure 10.2A).
```
```
Moreover, the three steps of the vinegar SSF fermentation (starch saccharifica-
```
```
tion, alcoholic fermentation, and AAF) are performed together in one fermentation
```
pot. The obtained Shanxi aged vinegar is of black-purple color, pleasant aroma, and
soft acid but not puckery taste. The Shanxi-Daqu is made from barley and pea by
spontaneous growth and metabolism of the microbes. It accounts for about 60% of
all raw materials for vinegar brewing, which contributes a lot to the complex flavors
and nutrient components of the Shanxi aged vinegar.
```
FIGURE 10.2 The flowchart of vinegar SSF process in China: (A) Shanxi aged vinegar;
```
```
(B) Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar; (C) Sichuan Baoning vinegar.
```
193Vinegar Production in China
Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar is most popular in Jiangnan. The original raw mate-
rial for the production of this vinegar was distillers’ grains of yellow wine, but
excellent quality sticky rice was adopted later as the raw material due to the limited
availability of distillers’ grains. Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar is fermented through
```
the traditional yellow wine brewing process for alcohol fermentation (i.e., though
```
```
saccharification and alcoholic fermentation through semi-solid culturing), solid-
```
```
state AAF, and over 3 months of ageing (Figure 10.2B). Besides, the starter Qu of
```
Zhenjiang vinegar fermentation consists of Xiaoqu and Maiqu, while other vinegars,
such as Shanxi aged vinegar and Sichuan Baoning vinegar, apply only one kind of
Qu for their fermentation. In addition, a cycle-inoculation style, in which the fermen-
```
tation culture of the 7th day is used as seed (starter) for the next round of inoculation,
```
is applied during the AAF process to propagate the microorganisms and efficiently
```
utilize the raw materials (Wang et al., 2015). This distinctive brewing technology
```
makes the Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar acidic but not astringent, fragrant and sweet,
with delicate color and taste, giving it a high reputation in China and worldwide.
Sichuan Baoning vinegar, as the most prestigious vinegar among Sichuan bran
vinegars, is named after the place of production and has a history of over a thousand
years. It is produced from uncooked wheat bran as the main raw material as well as
auxiliary and packing materials during the brewing process. Moreover, traditional
```
Chinese herbs are supplied to make herb Qu (originated from Xiaoqu) as starter to
```
```
initiate the fermentation (Figure 10.2C), such as Alpinia katsumadai, Eucommia
```
```
ulmoide, and Amomum villosum (Zhang et al., 2017). In addition, ternary simultane-
```
ous saccharification, alcoholic fermentation, and acetification are conducted, which
make these biochemical reactions hard to clearly distinguish. The end-product of
Sichuan Baoning vinegar has a red-brown color, soft sour taste, mellow and sweet
smell, and is an ideal and functional food seasoning.
10.4.2 liquid -state fermentation of CHinese Vinegar
As described in the previous chapters, there are two well-defined methods of vin-
egar LSF, namely, the slow, traditional static surface fermentation and the fast mod-
```
ern submerged fermentation, in which auxiliary materials are unnecessary (Haruta
```
```
et al., 2006; Tesfaye et al., 2002; Xu et al., 2010). In the static surface fermentation,
```
the oldest vinegar production method, the AAF is performed at the air–liquid inter-
face of a fermentable liquid. It is the most common manufacturing technology used
for the production of traditional oriental and Western vinegars. This technique is
inexpensive in terms of industrial investment, and the quality of the product is good
```
despite the rather long time required to achieve an efficient fermentation (Nanda
```
```
et al., 2001). The submerged fermentation method on the other hand is a state-of-the-
```
art technology used to produce vinegar at industrial scale and has several advantages
```
over other techniques (SSF or surface fermentation), such as the effective utilization
```
of raw materials, stable product quality, lower labor intensity, and high vinegar yield.
The modern vinegar industry benefits from the robust submerged fermentation pro-
```
cesses and has developed various optimization tools (Gullo et al., 2014); however,
```
there are still deficiencies in the end-product quality including poor vinegar color,
flavor, and taste compared vinegar brewed by SSF.
194 Advances in Vinegar Production
10.4.2.1 The Basic Technology of LSF
Generally, the static surface fermentation is carried out in appropriate covered fer-
mentation containers to conduct the alcoholic fermentation, which is considered a
good way to prevent bacterial contamination. Subsequently, AAF is performed when
the alcohol fermentation has finished, and a crepe pellicle of AAB covers the surface
```
of the liquid as the fermentation proceeds (Nanda et al., 2001). At this stage, the
```
oxygen supply relies only on the minimal contact between the liquid surface and the
air. Therefore, the height of the liquid in the fermentation vessel is reduced as much
as possible so as to increase the surface area per unit of liquid amount.
In China, “potiche,” or pot, is a relatively simple fermentation equipment com-
monly chosen to carry out the surface fermentation. During the whole fermentation
```
process, no strict sterilization measures and no pure strains are employed; instead the
```
```
microbes derive from the Qu, the air, and the containers (Murooka and Yamshita,
```
```
2008). In addition, the static surface fermentation method can be divided into pure-
```
liquid fermentation and solid–liquid mixing fermentation based on the composition
of the fermentation broth. Well-known Chinese Fuping millet vinegar, like French
traditional vinegar, Irish cider vinegar, and Spanish Sherry vinegar, is produced by
```
pure-liquid fermentation; while Zhejiang rose vinegar and Fujian Monascus vinegar,
```
```
like Japanese Fukuyama (a rice black vinegar), are brewed by solid–liquid mixing
```
```
fermentation (Murooka and Yamshita, 2008; Tesfaye et al., 2002). The latter technol-
```
ogy consists of diluting the fermentation broth to a certain concentration with water
after saccharification and alcoholic fermentation, followed by static surface AAF,
and finally obtaining the vinegar by separating the broth using the squeezing process
after the completion of AAF.
As described in the previous chapters, the industrial submerged vinegar fermen-
tation process consists of converting the alcohol in a fermented mash into acetic
acid under specific conditions by robust AAB and by supplying sterile air or oxygen
```
into the fermentation broth (Hromatka and Ebner, 1959). The submerged fermenta-
```
```
tion is mainly performed in semi-continuous mode (a repeated fed-batch process) to
```
obtain the highest possible yields of vinegar. This operation mode reduces the risk
```
of substrate inhibition and catabolite repression during fermentation (Gullo et al.,
```
```
2014). A widespread equipment for this type of fermentation is the Frings acetator as
```
described in more detail in Chapter 6. This equipment, with available automatic con-
```
trol, allows for the acetification of large volumes with a low air uptake (De Ory et al.,
```
```
1999; Sokollek et al., 1998). The availability of oxygen, acetic acid, ethanol, and
```
temperature are crucial factors for successful submerged fermentation processes.
Consequently, the vinegar production techniques of this type of fermentation have
```
been developed by optimizing process conditions and control (Gullo et al., 2014).
```
However, a major disadvantage is the loss of volatile compounds due to evaporation,
such as ethanol, acetic acid, or ethyl acetate, and the subsequent reduction of yield
by about 5–10%.
10.4.2.2 The Microflora of LSF
```
During the entire Zhejiang rose vinegar brewing process, the “Fahua” phase (the
```
```
starch saccharification) was found to be the most intense and complex phase regard-
```
```
ing microbial activity (Qiu et al., 2008). Molds were the main microorganisms in the
```
195Vinegar Production in China
early period of this phase, while yeasts and bacteria dominated in the intermediate
and later periods. Also, molds were mainly distributed on the surface of the culture
liquid during the whole phase. Bacteria and yeasts were mainly displayed in the
surface of the liquid during the early period and in the culture liquid during the
```
intermediate and later periods (Jiang et al., 2008).
```
```
Moreover, 43 strains of molds (including Penicillium icelandicum, Monascus
```
```
ruber, Aspergillus flavus, and Penicillium plicas), nine strains of yeasts (including
```
```
Saccharomyces boulardii, S. cerevisiae, and Kluyveromyces marxianus), and 16
```
```
strains bacteria (six of them were A. pasteurians) were detected during the Zhejiang
```
rose vinegar fermentation process. Other dominant bacteria included Gluconobacter
```
oxydans and LAB (Leuconostoc mesenteroides, and the Lactobacillus species L.
```
```
reuteri, L. bulgaricus, L. acidophilus, and L. casei). Furthermore, Jiang et al. (2010)
```
reported that bioaugmentation of L. plantarum and S. cerevisiae in the production
of Zhenjiang rose vinegar could greatly enhance the content of lactic acid during the
alcoholic fermentation stage and improve the flavor of the product.
In addition, Gluconacetobacter xylinus was reported to have a high acetic acid
productivity during the surface fermentation to produce the traditional Cantonese
rice vinegar in China, which may be explained by the fact that the structure of the
cellulosic membrane synthesized by these bacteria supports the cells close to the
```
air–liquid interface facilitating the oxygen uptake (Fu et al., 2014).
```
The investigation of the microbial flora during the Fujian Monascus vinegar
fermentation process showed that more AAB species in this vinegar were dis-
played than in rose vinegar, including Acetobacter aceti, Acetobacter methanolica,
```
Gluconacetobacter swingsii, Gluconacetobacter europaeus (now Komagataeibacter
```
```
europaeus), and LAB including Lactobacillus hilgardii, L. casei, and L. helveticus
```
```
(Yamada et al., 2012; Yan et al., 2017).
```
According to previous studies, the indigenous bacterial population for vinegar-
making during submerged fermentation seems quite homogeneous, involving mainly
Gluconacetobacter and Acetobacter since they exert a strong tolerance to high acetic
```
acid concentration (Kittelmann et al., 1989; Sievers et al., 1992). Specifically, strains
```
of G. europaeus isolated from industrial vinegar bioreactors can tolerate acetic acid
```
concentrations up to 100 g/L (Trcek et al., 2007), while A. aceti can grow at acetic
```
```
acid concentrations exceeding 70 g/L in continuous cultivation (Yong et al., 1989).
```
However, A. pasteurianus and A. aceti, possessing a strong oxidative activity against
```
ethanol, are mostly found in low acidity vinegars (∼6%). G. europaeus is isolated
```
from low acidity vinegars during the processing phase with constant acetic acid
content.
10.4.2.3 The Representative Vinegars of LSF
Traditionally, Zhejiang rose vinegar is made from rice as raw material, using natural
microorganisms in the geographical environment of Zhejiang, and is brewed by the
solid “Fahua” phase and the liquid static surface fermentation principle without add-
```
ing any colorings (Figure 10.3A). The source of microorganisms in the fermentation
```
```
of rose vinegar is mainly from the cover of the container (made with hay and called
```
```
“Caogai” in Chinese) (Miao et al., 2006). The general production period of this
```
vinegar starts at the suitable temperature and humidity season of the local climate,
196 Advances in Vinegar Production
namely mid-April to mid-July, and has a long ageing period and production cycle to
form a typical color and mouthfeel.
Rose vinegar is very common in the Jiangsu and Zhejiang areas and is different
from ordinary vinegar, with a unique bright and transparent rose red color, pure vin-
egar aroma, and a soft and lasting sour taste with a slight sweetness.
Fujian Monascus vinegar is based on the raw materials of sticky rice, late-
season rice, Hongqu white sugar, and sesame and is brewed using a unique liq-
```
uid circulation process (Figure 10.3B). It adopts a technology in which rice and
```
high-quality mature vinegar are gradually added to the steamed rice in order to
enrich various types of microorganisms and takes about three years to obtain
mother culture of Fujian Monascus vinegar. The liquid circulation brewing pro-
cess of the Fujian Monascus vinegar consists of continuously removing mature
Fujian Monascus vinegar from the jar with the mother culture every year and at
```
the same time adding an equal volume of Fujian Monascus liquor (the product of
```
```
alcoholic fermentation). Based on this brewing process, the microflora that pro-
```
duces acetic acid and other aroma substances is enriched, and a stable and reli-
able amount of the mother culture can be preserved for a long term by stirring
every day. This continuous brewing process can lead to the production of high-
quality Fujian Monascus vinegar. During the long-term ageing, sesame is soaked
in the vinegar, conferring sesame flavor and sesame lignans to the end-product.
```
FIGURE 10.3 The flowchart of vinegar LSF process in China: (A) Zhejiang rose vinegar;
```
```
(B) Fujian Monascus vinegar.
```

Moreover, this vinegar produced in the Yongchun County has a sweet and acid
taste, high content of non-volatile acids, and is well-known inside and outside the
province and Southeast Asia.
10.5 NEW TRENDS
With the improvement of living standards, people’s awareness on health care has
gradually increased in China. The market demand for vinegar is also growing since
the products that use vinegar as a seasoning and raw material have been favored by
```
the market (Wu and Lan, 2012). However, the vinegar industry in China is one of the
```
industries with relatively slow development and plays a “small product” role among
the condiment industries, and still has some shortcomings regarding the traditional
production processes that need to be solved.
10.5.1 tHe researCH of BasiC Vinegar produCtion prinCiples
Although the scale of the vinegar industry in China has expanded, the production
technology of the traditional vinegar still relies on the accumulation of practical
experience. There are several difficulties in the transformation of the traditional
vinegar brewing, and major breakthroughs in key technologies are required. A sci-
entifically based dissecting of the mechanisms underlying the microbial communi-
ties formation and function is pivotal in traditional vinegar brewing. The in-depth
research on the basic principles of vinegar production, including the pattern and
functionality of the microbial populations and the flavor generation mechanisms,
are scarce.
Current applications of culture-dependent and culture-independent approaches
have provided a blueprint of microbial diversity in the vinegar ecosystems for
Shanxi aged vinegar, Zhenjiang aromatic vinegar, Tianjin Duliu mature vinegar, and
```
Shaanxi Qishan vinegar (Li et al., 2016b; Nie et al., 2013, 2015; Wu et al., 2012a,
```
```
2017). Further study on the functionality of microbiota in vinegar fermentation
```
through metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and metaproteomics, is the trend to
resolve their metabolic contributions and to promote the vinegar production pro-
cess. In addition, the microbial dynamic responses to the spontaneous fermentation
parameters are another important area for further study. The environmental fac-
tors during the vinegar fermentation process are investigated in increasing reports
```
recently, aiming at improving the technical aspects of vinegar production (Li et al.,
```
```
2015a, 2016a).
```
In China, traditional vinegar production faces low utilization of raw materials and
production efficiency. Screening of high cellulase-producing microorganisms, that
are particularly suitable for SSF to generate acetic acid, can contribute to the com-
plete utilization of the raw materials. For LSF, the use of pure AAB cultures with a
high acid production capacity can also improve the utilization of the raw materials.
However, generally LSF leads to the production of lower quality vinegar. Therefore,
multi-species fermentation and excellent yeasts and AAB for LSF must be further
investigated for improving the yield and quality of vinegar.
198 Advances in Vinegar Production
10.5.2 quality eValuation and safety Control in Vinegar produCtion
The quality assessment of Chinese vinegar has been receiving more and more atten-
tion since people gradually pursue high-quality and safe vinegar products in China
```
(Chen et al., 2012). The national standard in China stipulates four sensory charac-
```
teristics of vinegar: color, fragrance, taste, and body. Obviously, these standards are
not comprehensive and scientific criteria for vinegar evaluation. Just like the estab-
lishment of a “fingerprint library” for Chinese liquor, the chemical composition of
vinegar will be used to describe the characteristics of vinegar and identify different
```
brands of vinegar by sophisticated equipment (e.g., electronic nose). The vinegar pro-
```
duction enterprises should introduce advanced management experience to gradually
```
implement Good Agricultural Production Practices (GAP), Good Manufacturing
```
```
Practices (GMP), Hazard Analysis and Critical Control Point systems (HACCP) in
```
the raw materials, the production, processing, and storage methods, as well as on
```
the transportation and sales (Zhang et al., 2015). To supervise the whole vinegar
```
production process and to ensure the quality and safety of the product, it is necessary
to establish Food Defense according to the practical situation of Chinese vinegar
production.
10.5.3 researCH on tHe diVerse funCtionality of Vinegar
With the scientific research revealing the functional properties of vinegar, the con-
sumption of vinegar has been expanded from the seasoning vinegar, to the beverage
vinegar, to the health promoting vinegar. According to research reports on the func-
tional components and flavor substances in traditional cereal vinegar, vinegar prod-
ucts functional for lowering blood fat, lowering blood pressure, enhancing immunity,
and treating fatigue have been developed.
The diversification of vinegar products is a new trend in the vinegar industry. In
recent years, many domestic manufacturers have improved the brewing process by
using local special animal and plant origin raw materials and modern biotechnol-
ogy to produce a large number of new functional vinegar products, including jujube
black vinegar, low polyxylose cherry vinegar, oligosaccharide rose vinegar series,
fermented aloe vinegar drink, bitter buckwheat vinegar, pear fruit vinegar, fructus
momordicae vinegar, kiwi fruit vinegar, tomato vinegar, sea buckthorn fruit vinegar,
```
fig vinegar, onion vinegar, wild jujube health vinegar, and bamboo vinegar (Mao,
```
```
2013). The vinegar industry has also availed by increasing the size of fruit vinegar
```
production. With the continuous research on the composition and application val-
ues of vinegar, it is believed that the functional effects of vinegar in the future will
be more fully excavated, and the modern medicinal science technology will fur-
ther exploit them to have an impact on both vinegar production and the health care
market.
10.5.4 equipment for Vinegar produCtion
The improvement of vinegar production cannot be separated from the updating of
vinegar equipment. The traditional vinegar production equipment includes mainly
199Vinegar Production in China
potiche, barrels, and pots in China, resulting in low industrialization and single prod-
```
ucts (Liang and Li, 2012). With the rapid growth of the vinegar industry, the equip-
```
ment has also been developing in the direction of mechanized, large-scale production
```
(Zou et al., 2017). In the past 30 years, some manufacturers have gradually improved
```
the backward containers and tools of the different fermentation stages, replacing the
```
vats (pottery) and pools (concrete), with pools and tanks (stainless steel), respec-
```
tively. Moreover, mechanical tumbling and grabbing equipment, large-scale alco-
holic fermentation equipment, high-pressure equipment for smoked vinegar Pei, etc.,
```
for mechanized upgrading have been adopted (Wenfeng, 2018).
```
However, difficulties in scale-up are related to the massive heat generation and
inhomogeneity of the SSF systems. Under aerobic conditions, the microbial growth
generates considerable heat leading to a fast increase of temperature. This effect is
undesirable, especially in some biotechnological processes that involve heat-sensitive
microbes or enzymes. Several bioreactors have been designed in an attempt to com-
```
bat these problems, but only a few have been used at large scale; more large-scale
```
bioreactors are anticipated to be adopted in the future.
The advanced technologies applied in food machinery include microelectron-
ics, optoelectronics, vacuum, membrane separation, extrusion puffing, microwave,
ultrafine grinding, supercritical extraction, sterilization, and intelligent technolo-
gies. These technologies are helpful in promoting the modernization of the vinegar
industry. The development and introduction of advanced technologies, equipment,
and new materials, as well as the development of independent domestic innovation
equipment and computer control equipment, are also major development trends in
the Chinese vinegar industry. These developments will enable the vinegar produc-
tion enterprises to speed up the computer-to-production processes and the automatic
control equipment management and will promote the overall improvement of pro-
duction efficiency.
According to some reports, annual per capita consumption of vinegar in Japan is
```
about 3.5 times that of China (Zou et al., 2017). Hence, China’s vinegar industry has
```
a broad market space and development prospects. The scale of small and medium-
```
sized enterprises (SMEs) will be integrated and the old production mode and frame-
```
work will be changed. The process of development towards vinegar enterprise
groups will be further accelerated. Moreover, the vinegar industry will move toward
the development of automation, standardization, and branding and explore new mod-
els suitable for the development of the China’s vinegar industry in the future.

11.1 INTRODUCTION
As discussed in more details in previous chapters, historically, vinegar production
has been associated with the spontaneous fermentation of natural crops, depending
on the agricultural development in the different parts of the world. In the beginning,
vinegar was naturally formed from several raw materials such as fruit or cereals. The
microorganisms that colonized the stored products after ripening firstly produced
alcohol and then acetic acid. Vinegar has been considered a valuable product, used
